resolution: The prima via itself defines moving as educing from potency to act (claim AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-REDUCED-BY-A-MOVER-A), and the case reads motus in that broad sense. Aristotle's physical change is one kind of such reduction, so the observation premise STMT-SOMETHING-IS-MOVED-IN-THIS-WORLD holds on either reading. All premises share `MovedIn`/`MovesIn` over an abstract `Respect`, so the formal results hold for any one reading applied throughout; an objection that the regress premises hold only for local motion is an objection to a premise, not an equivocation. The typed Physics readings (TruthCore.Greek.Aristotle.Physics.Typed, docs/typed-physics.md) read the same `MovedIn`/`MovesIn` as Aristotle's physical change; the results that combine them with prima via premises (for example ARIST-PHYS-VIII-4-EVERY-MOVED-HAS-A-PER-SE-MOVER, ARIST-PHYS-VII-1-REGRESS-FROM-PER-SE-REGRESS) apply both premise sets to that one reading, which is one kind of reduction from potency to act, so no step passes from one sense to the other.
